newsitem.title: LEBANON: Hizbollah fighter killed in Israeli air raid.
newsitem.headline: Hizbollah fighter killed in Israeli air raid.

text.p: A Hizbollah guerrilla was killed and four wounded on Saturday when Israeli jets rocketed their training camp close to the Lebanese-Syrian border, Hizbollah sources said.
Lebanese security sources said Israeli F-16 jets fired two rockets into the base at Janta in the Syrian-policed Bekaa Valley.
The training camp, for pro-Iranian Hizbollah guerrillas, is located near the village of Nabi Sheet, some five km (three miles) from the border.
Hizbollah sources said a rocket hit a base for anti-aircraft weapons near the camp.
An Israeli army spokesman confirmed the attack -- the 50th air assault into Lebanon this year.
"Israeli aircraft attacked an operational base of Hizbollah in the area of Janta south of Baalbek," the spokesman said. "Pilots reported scoring accurate hits and all planes returned safely to base."
A day earlier, Israeli warplanes attacked Palestinian bases south of Beirut after Katyusha rockets slammed into northern Israel, wounding an Israeli woman.

The attacks came amid the worst cross-border tensions between Lebanon and Israel in more than 15 months after Israel launched a 17-day April blitz on the country in 1996, killing some 200 people -- mostly civilians.
Between Monday and Thursday, 13 Lebanese -- including seven civilians -- were killed by bombs, Israeli shelling and rocket attacks.
Saturday's air raid brought to six the number of Hizbollah guerrillas killed in Israeli attacks in less than a week. On Monday, Israeli commandos killed five fighters with a roadside bomb.
The Moslem militant Hizbollah group, fighting to oust Israeli troops from a 15-km (nine-mile)-wide south Lebanon occupation zone, said it did not fire the Katyusha rockets on Friday.
However, its chief Sheikh Hassan Nasrallah threatened to resume Katyusha rocketing of northern Israel because a 1996 U.S.-brokered ceasefire understanding ceased to protect Lebanese civilians.
"We say the resumption of using other means to protect civilians has become necessary," he said.
Under the terms of the understanding which ended the blitz last year, Hizbollah and Israeli troops are barred from targeting civilians on both sides of the borders.
